meta.status: INDICATIVE, NOT VALIDATED: APSIM-X process-model output, not calibrated for this site.
meta.note: APSIM scenario numbers exist only for Mambang Muda, North Sumatra, Indonesia and are precomputed; prices are yours; indicative, not validated; no savings or ROI claim.

weather_variants.as_delivered: Open-Meteo rain as delivered (about +35% vs the founder's station in the 2013-2022 overlap)
weather_variants.rain_scaled: Open-Meteo rain from 2023 multiplied by the station/Open-Meteo ratio of the overlap years (sensitivity, not a calibration)

inputs.name: ffb_price_per_tonne
inputs.note: price you receive for fresh fruit bunches

inputs.name: n_price_per_kg
inputs.note: cost of fertiliser per kg of nitrogen (product price per kg / N fraction; e.g. urea is 46% N)

inputs.name: water_price_per_m3
inputs.note: cost of irrigation water per m3 (1 mm over 1 ha = 10 m3)

inputs.name: irrigation_fixed_cost_per_ha_year
inputs.unit: currency units per ha per year
inputs.note: irrigation operating cost that applies only when the scenario irrigates at all (0 = not counted)

inputs.name: harvest_haul_cost_per_tonne
inputs.note: extra harvest/transport cost per extra tonne of FFB (0 = not counted)

evaluation.partial_year: year after the last full year, up to the last day of the weather file (includes forecast days); NOT a full year, do not annualise
evaluation.weather_note: 2023-2025 weather is a HINDCAST (Open-Meteo archive, grid cell near the site); it is not a forecast of future seasons. Annual FFB needs a full year, which is why a hindcast window is used.
evaluation.planting_year_note: ASSUMED (founder's 2001 planting breaks the model beyond ~25 y). Palm age in 2023-2025 is about 11-14 y under this assumption.

exist_and_varied_here.how: multiplier on every N rate in the founder's 'Palm Management' manager code, from 2023 (the founder's code sets rates by palm age; amounts are hard-coded there)
3 doses (15 Jan/May/Sep, founder) vs 6 equal doses (15 Jan/Mar/May/Jul/Sep/Nov)
the founder's file contains an Irrigation model but nothing applies water; we ADD a rule-based manager (trigger on fw, fixed mm, minimum days between)

do_not_exist: phosphorus and potassium fertiliser (the model simulates N only)
a dedicated leaching-prevention practice (cover crop, slow-release N, drainage control): leaching is only an OUTPUT; the only levers that influence it are the N rate and N splitting above
irrigation scheduling beyond the simple rule we add (no soil-moisture sensors, no forecast-driven rule)

units.ffb_t_ha_yr: t fresh fruit bunch per ha per calendar year: sum of the model's per-harvest 'HarvestFFB' ([Units("t/ha")], from the OilPalm model source) added up by the founder's manager as Calculations.Script.AnnualYield (report column 'Calculations.Script.AnnualYield' in AnnualOutput)
units.n_leached_no3_kg_ha: kg NO3-N per ha leached below the 2 m profile (sum of [Soil].SoilWater.LeachNO3: 'amount of N leaching as NO3-N from the deepest soil layer')
units.irrigation_mm: mm applied (sum of [Irrigation].IrrigationApplied); 1 mm over 1 ha = 10 m3
units.drainage_mm: mm drained below the profile (sum of [Soil].SoilWater.Drainage)

formulas: d_ffb_t_ha = FFB_scenario - FFB_base   (APSIM-X, mean of the full hindcast years)
d_extra_harvest_haul_cost = d_ffb_t_ha * harvest_haul_cost_per_tonne   (0 unless you set it)
d_water_cost = (irrigation_mm_scenario - irrigation_mm_base) * 10 m3 per mm per ha * water_price_per_m3
d_irrigation_fixed_cost = fixed cost if the scenario irrigates (mm > 0) minus the same for the base
net_difference = d_revenue - d_extra_harvest_haul_cost - d_fertiliser_cost - d_water_cost - d_irrigation_fixed_cost
break_even_ffb_price = harvest_haul_cost + (d_fert + d_water + d_fixed) / d_ffb   (price at which net = 0; undefined when d_ffb = 0)

break_even_yield_factor f: net(f) = f * d_ffb * (ffb_price - harvest_haul_cost) - (d_fert + d_water + d_fixed) = 0  ->  f = (d_fert + d_water + d_fixed) / (d_ffb * (ffb_price - harvest_haul_cost)); f = 1 means APSIM-X's response as simulated
sensitivity 'unfavourable': FFB price x (1 - p), all cost prices x (1 + p); 'favourable': the reverse; p = sensitivity_pct/100
yield what-if: d_ffb multiplied by (1 - w), 1, (1 + w) with w = yield_whatif_pct/100; an illustration of a wrong response, NOT an error estimate

scenarios.label: Base (founder's management)
scenarios.description: Founder's N schedule unchanged (about 158.8 kg N/ha/yr at maturity, 3 doses 15 Jan/May/Sep), no irrigation.

scenarios.label: N fertiliser 0.5x
scenarios.description: Half the founder's N rate from 2023, same dates, no irrigation.

break_even.reading: scenario better than base when the FFB price is BELOW the break-even price (it loses yield but saves cost); and better than base if the real yield loss is smaller than 0.198 x the simulated change (at the ffb price given)

scenarios.label: N fertiliser 1.5x
scenarios.description: 1.5 times the founder's N rate from 2023, same dates, no irrigation.

break_even.reading: scenario better than base when the FFB price is ABOVE the break-even price; and better than base if the real yield gain is at least 0.392 x the simulated change (at the ffb price given)

scenarios.label: Same N, 6 doses/yr
scenarios.description: Founder's annual N rate split into 6 equal doses (15 Jan/Mar/May/Jul/Sep/Nov) instead of 3, no irrigation. The only leaching-related lever the model offers besides the N rate.

break_even.reading: no cost difference: the sign of d_ffb alone decides, no break-even exists

scenarios.label: Water top-up when fw < 0.9
scenarios.description: Founder's N. Rule: if yesterday's fw < 0.9 and 3+ days since the last top-up, apply 10 mm.

break_even.reading: no positive FFB price makes net zero: worse than base at every price (less yield and higher cost); no positive yield-response factor gives net zero

scenarios.label: Water top-up when fw < 0.8
scenarios.description: Founder's N. Rule: if yesterday's fw < 0.8 and 3+ days since the last top-up, apply 10 mm.

break_even.reading: scenario better than base when the FFB price is ABOVE the break-even price; and better than base if the real yield gain is at least 4.12 x the simulated change (at the ffb price given)

limitations: APSIM-X yield response is UNVALIDATED for this site: the founder's model has no Sumatra calibration, no comparison with measured FFB, and only N (no P/K) is modelled. Treat deltas as model behaviour, not as measured response.
Palm age is ASSUMED (planted 2012-01-01 in the model copy; the founder's 2001 planting breaks the model beyond about 25 years).

Weather 2023-2025 is a hindcast from Open-Meteo (about +35% more rain than the founder's station in the overlap years); the rain_scaled variant shows how much the answer depends on that. It is not a forecast of future seasons.

The yield response is not instantaneous in the model: with N 1.5x the first year (2023) differs from base by about 0 t/ha and the gain appears in 2024-2025, so a 3-year mean mixes a lag period with the response (cause, probably bunch development time, not verified). The per-year table shows this; a longer window was not run.
One point only (Mambang Muda), one soil, one management schedule hard-coded in the founder's manager (rates by palm age, 14-day harvest).

Differences of about 1 t FFB/ha over three years or less are within what harvest timing and small model changes alone produce (for example splitting the same N into 6 doses changes 3-year FFB by about 1%); do not read them as real effects.

Prices are your inputs. Defaults are placeholders ('example, replace with your costs'), not market data. Not counted: capital and installation cost, labour, N application cost, discounting, price risk, other nutrients, environmental value of reduced leaching.
No savings, profit or return-on-investment claim is made or implied. 'net_difference' is a per-hectare yearly difference between two model scenarios, nothing more.
